proposals.before: The relevant office memorialized to compose suburban and temple hymns; the emperor ordered Chancellor Chu Yuan, attendant Xie Tiao, attendant at leisure Kong Zhigui, Erudite Wang Xuanzhi, Zongming scholars Liu Rong, He Fajiong, and He Yanxiu — ten in all — to compose; only Chaozong's hymn was used.
proposals.after: The relevant office memorialized to compose suburban and temple hymns; the emperor ordered Chancellor Chu Yuan, attendant Xie Fei, attendant at leisure Kong Zhigui, Erudite Wang Xuanzhi, Zongming scholars Liu Rong, He Fajiong, and He Tanxiu — ten in all — to compose; only Chaozong's hymn was used.
proposals.reason: 謝朏 is Xie Fei, not Xie Tiao (謝朓); 何曇秀 is He Tanxiu, not He Yanxiu.

proposals.before: Your prisoner entered office twenty-odd years from coarse cloth, sunk in hardship without heaven's clarity.
proposals.after: When the imperial fortune was first established, he was plucked up — sacrifice officer and chief clerk, both in the former dynasty's chancellor offices.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English duplicates s0206 instead of translating 皇運初基，便蒙抽擢，祭酒主簿，竝皆先朝相府.

decisions.reason: Chinese 侍中謝朏 and 何曇秀 require Xie Fei and He Tanxiu; Xie Tiao and He Yanxiu misread those graphs, and the proposed literal otherwise matches the unit.
Unit s0184 is only 故破山之雷，不發聾夫之耳; the blind-eye English belongs to the next unit, and the proposed clause restores this couplet half accurately.
